findings: Escalation lift on ambiguous cases is only 1.167x over decisive cases, while 86% of decisive cases escalate too. Escalation is close to uniform, so correctly escalating the ambiguous cases is weak evidence of judgement - a system that escalated everything would score the same on that measure.

Overall escalation rate is 87%. In production that is roughly 20 human reviews per 23 flagged payments, which is a staffing cost, not a free safety margin. Auto-decision quality below should be read against it.

infrastructure_failures.meaning: Transport or provider failures. These say nothing about agent reasoning quality and any metric computed over a run containing them is measured on degraded evidence.

agent_protocol_failures.meaning: The agent ran but did not produce a usable structured result (bad tool call, turn limit, tool execution error). A reasoning-adjacent failure, distinct from both infrastructure and from being wrong.

wrong_auto_decisions.meaning: The system ran correctly and committed to the wrong answer. This is the only bucket that measures reasoning quality, and it is the one that matters.

escalated_decisive_cases.meaning: Cases with a clear ground truth that the system would not commit to. Not wrong, but not autonomous either - each one is a human review the system failed to save.

ablation_study.method: Re-runs the supervisor's aggregation and decision functions over a reduced panel using the findings already recorded in the event log. No additional model calls, so this measures the decision logic exactly as it ran.

precedent_dependence.why_this_matters: The precedent corpus and the case bank were authored by the same person, so the historical-case specialist has a contamination advantage that would not survive contact with a real case archive. Decisions that depend on it should be discounted accordingly.

concerns: RUN MODE: live tool-use loops via openai_compat:api.groq.com on openai/gpt-oss-20b. Specialist and supervisor reasoning is model-driven, so re-running will not reproduce these numbers exactly, and results are specific to this provider and model - a different model on the same code would score differently. Single-run results at this sample size should be treated as indicative.

SAMPLE SIZE: 23 cases, 21 with a decisive ground truth. Every per-category figure below rests on 2-7 cases. Confidence intervals at that size are wide enough to swallow most of the differences between categories, and none of these numbers would survive being quoted as a production benchmark.

AUTONOMY: 87% of cases were escalated to a human. High precision on the remaining auto-decisions is partly a selection effect - the system chose which cases to be judged on. A fraud team would not deploy this without pushing the escalation rate down, and doing so is exactly what would expose the error rate this report cannot currently see.

MULTI-SIGNAL REASONING: only 67% of auto-decisions survive removal of their loudest specialist. The rest collapse to a different verdict, which means the four-specialist architecture is not earning its cost on those cases - a single specialist plus the threshold logic would have produced the same answers.

RETRIEVAL CONTAMINATION: 1 auto-decision(s) change when the historical-case specialist is removed. The precedent corpus was written alongside the case bank by the same author, and retrieval is lexical TF-IDF, so precedent summaries share vocabulary with the cases they 'predict'. Retrieval hits at this rate would not transfer to a real case archive, and any per-category strength that traces back to this specialist should be discounted.

FAILURE ACCOUNTING: 80 infrastructure failure(s) and 5 agent-protocol failure(s) occurred, against 1 genuinely wrong auto-decision(s). These are reported apart because they mean different things: infrastructure failures make the metrics less reliable, protocol failures point at prompt or schema problems, and only the last bucket is evidence about reasoning quality.

NOT MEASURED: the case bank was written by the same person who wrote the detectors, so it encodes the same assumptions about what fraud looks like. Nothing here tests the patterns neither the author nor the agents thought of, and that blind spot is where a real fraud system's losses actually come from. Adversarial cases authored by someone else would be the first thing to add.
honesty_and_self_scrutiny.how_to_read_this: Read the escalation rate first, then the escalation_as_flag false-positive rate, then the ablation study. The auto_only precision figure is the least informative number in this report and is printed first only because that is the convention.
